meta.title: Aphantasia and hyperphantasia: exploring imagery vividness extremes
meta.domain: Cognitive neuroscience — mental imagery vividness extremes (review)
meta.overview: Narrative review of aphantasia (absent/markedly reduced voluntary imagery) and hyperphantasia (perception-like vivid imagery) as the extremes of imagery vividness — prevalence, familial aggregation, associations with memory/face-recognition/autism, preserved visual dreaming, and candidate neural substrates in frontoparietal-visual connectivity.
meta.abstract: The vividness of imagery varies between individuals. The existence of people with markedly reduced or absent wakeful imagery was neglected until the coinage of 'aphantasia'; 'hyperphantasia' denotes imagery rivalling perception. Around 1% and 3% of the population experience extreme aphantasia and hyperphantasia. Aphantasia runs in families, often affects several sense modalities, and is variably associated with reduced autobiographical memory, face-recognition difficulty, and autism, while visual dreaming is often preserved. Altered connectivity between frontoparietal and visual networks may provide the neural substrate for imagery extremes.

claims.statement: Aphantasia (~1%) and hyperphantasia (~3%) exist as extremes of imagery vividness in the general population.
Aphantasia is variably associated with reduced autobiographical memory.
Aphantasia is associated with increased likelihood of face-recognition difficulty.
Aphantasia aggregates in families (elevated sibling recurrence).
Altered connectivity between frontoparietal and visual networks provides the neural substrate for imagery extremes.

contributions.typing_rationale: Explicitly a Trends in Cognitive Sciences review synthesizing behavioural, physiological, and neural evidence on aphantasia and hyperphantasia into a unified account of imagery vividness extremes.

sota.resolver_notes: Undermind semantic search (year_max=2024) placed this review directly downstream of the author's own prior work: Zeman 2020 (Phantasia) is the closest prior review, Milton 2021 supplies the behavioural/neural signatures, and Kay 2022 the physiological index it summarizes. A 2024 7T-fMRI study (Liu 2024) is a contemporaneous empirical neighbour. As a synthesis of a maturing field, finding-level overlap with its priors is high.
